title: FBI Probes Alaska Senate Race Over Dual 'Dan Sullivans' on the Ballot
snippet: Federal agents are questioning donors in Alaska following allegations that a second candidate named Dan Sullivan was added to the Senate ballot to confuse voters.
content:
ANCHORAGE, Alaska — Federal investigators are turning up the heat on Alaska's high-stakes U.S. Senate race, reaching out to donors of candidate Dan J. Sullivan to determine whether supporters were tricked into funding a second candidate who shares the exact name of Republican incumbent Sen. Dan Sullivan.

On Friday, an FBI agent visited a boat dealership in the remote community of Petersburg, Alaska, attempting to contact donor Charles Flint. Flint, who contributed $500 to Dan J. Sullivan—a local retired teacher and musician—said he was completely aware of who he was backing. "I don’t feel like I’ve been misled at all," Flint said, adding that Alaskans are fully capable of telling the candidates apart in the state's ranked-choice voting system.

Federal Intervention and Campaign Fallout

The FBI's field visits follow confirmation of an active federal criminal inquiry. U.S. Attorney Michael Heyman stated that federal authorities deployed a surge of law enforcement assets to Alaska after media reports suggested Democratic challenger Mary Peltola's campaign may have been involved in recruiting the second Dan Sullivan. Concurrently, the U.S. Department of Justice is petitioning a court to segregate certain Alaska ballots to examine potential voter confusion.

Peltola, a former congresswoman challenging Sen. Sullivan in Tuesday's election, forcefully rejected the accusations during a campaign rally in Anchorage. She called the claims "garbage" and described them as a coordinated smear campaign aimed at dampening voter turnout. "I know I can beat Dan Sullivan. I do not need any help winning this race," Peltola told volunteers.
